LOCATION.-I sec. 9, T. 36 N., R. 2 E., half a mile above Lindsay Flat, Shasta County, 3 miles below mouth of Rock Creek and 11 miles below Pecks Bridge.
RECORDS AVAILABLE.-November 1, 1922, to September 30, 1925. Gage.-Water-stage - recorder on right bank one-fourth mile above Pit No. 3 power house.

chunks.content:
# SURFACE WATER SUPPLY, 1925, PART XI (cont.)

## PIT RIVER AT LINDSAY FLAT, CALIF. (cont.)

DISCHARGE MEASUREMENTS.-Made from cable about 250 feet below gage. CHANNEL AND CONTROL.-Rough, rocky, strewn with boulders; practically permanent. One channel at all stages; banks not subject to overflow.

EXTREMES OF DISCHARGE.-Maximum stage during year, from water-stage recorder, 8.64 feet 7 to 10 p.m. February 6 (discharge, 6,460 second-feet); minimum stage, 1.12 feet during afternoon of September 18 (discharge, 77 second-feet).

1923-1925: Maximum stage from water-stage recorder, that of February 6, 1925; minimum stage, that of September 18, 1925.

Ice.-Stage-discharge relation not affected by ice.

DIVERSIONS.-The: are numerous irrigation diversions from Pit River and tributaries above gage, and beginning June 18, 1925, varying amounts have been stored and diverted for Pit No. 3 development.

REGULATION.-The flow is completely regulated at Pit No. 3 dam during low and medium stages.

ACCuRaCY.-Stage-discharge relation practically permanent. Rating curve well defined. Daily discharge ascertained by applying mean daily gage height to rating table, except October 7-14, 29, and 30, for which it was estimated by comparison with records for other Pit River stations. Records excellent.

COOPERATION.-Gage-height record and the results of discharge measurements furnished by Mount Shasta Power Corporation.
